newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hijacker overpowered on Austrian plane in Berlin.
newsitem.headline: Hijacker overpowered on Austrian plane in Berlin.

text.p: An Austrian Airlines plane bound for Vienna was hijacked on Tuesday, but police said the attack ended when the hijacker was overpowered shortly after the plane returned to Berlin's Tegel airport.
Flight 0S 104, carrying 28 passengers and five crew, was heading for Vienna from the German capital when it was hijacked and forced to return to Berlin.
It was not immediately clear how the hijack was staged or whether the attacker, believed to be a lone assailant, was carrying a weapon.
"It has ended peacefully. No one has been harmed," a spokeswoman for Austrian Airlines told Reuters in Vienna. "The hijacker was overpowered."
Austrian news agency APA said the hijacker was seized two minutes after the plane touched down and was arrested.
German police provided sketchy details and were initially reluctant call it a hijacking. "We have an unscheduled landing at this time," a spokeswoman said.
Officials could not immediately confirm reports that the plane was hijacked in airspace over the Czech Republic.
Vienna lies some 900 km (550 miles) south of Berlin. Normal flying time is about two hours.
